variants.omim_name: KIF1B, INHERITED LOSS-OF-FUNCTION KIF1BBETA MISSENSE MUTATIONS
MAX, FIVE DIFFERENT MUTATIONS IN THE MAX GENE
as_reported: five different mutations in the MAX gene

records.label: Patients with neuroblastoma or pheochromocytoma carrying inherited KIF1Bbeta mutations
quotes: We identified inherited loss-of-function KIF1Bbeta missense mutations in neuroblastomas and pheochromocytomas and an acquired loss-of-function mutation in a medulloblastoma, arguing that KIF1Bbeta is a pathogenic target of these deletions.

records.label: Three unrelated exome-sequenced hereditary PCC cases

phenotypes.text: absence of MAX protein in tumors

quotes: We sequenced the exomes of three unrelated individuals with hereditary PCC (cases) and identified mutations in MAX, the MYC associated factor X gene.
Absence of MAX protein in the tumors and loss of heterozygosity caused by uniparental disomy supported the involvement of MAX alterations in the disease.

records.label: Follow-up series of 59 selected PCC cases with MAX mutations
quotes: A follow-up study of a selected series of 59 cases with PCC identified five additional MAX mutations and suggested an association with malignant outcome and preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations.

records.label: Six consecutive patients with MAX-related pheochromocytoma

phenotypes.text: multiple pheochromocytomas within the same gland

variants.as_reported: five different mutations in the MAX gene

quotes: in six consecutive patients (four at the initial diagnosis and two at the follow-up evaluation) with rare, but clinically important, MAX-related PHEOs

The patients had five different mutations in the MAX gene that caused disruption of Max/Myc interaction and/or abolished interaction with DNA based on in silico analyses. All but one patient developed bilateral PHEOs during their lifetime.
The two PHEOs missed on 18F-FDOPA PET/CT were <1 cm, corresponding to nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia.

records.label: III-3
records.segregation: MAX variant shared with affected grandfather and sister and with uncle; loss of WT MAX allele in both PCCs; KIF1B variant absent
quotes: The proband’s youngest brother (III-3) presented at 31 years with a cardiomyopathy complicated by a Takotsubo’s syndrome which led to the diagnosis of bilateral PCC.
The only heterozygous variant identified was in MAX (NM_002382.5): c.145T>C, p.Ser49Pro.
we analyzed the tumor DNAs of patient III-3 and identified loss of the MAX WT allele in both tumors (Fig. 3) suggesting that this variant is indeed responsible for the bilateral PCC in this patient.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: III-1 (proband)

phenotypes.text: bilateral pheochromocytoma (right at 22 y, left 6 years later)

records.segregation: MAX and KIF1B variants inherited paternally; no LOH of MAX WT allele in her PCCs; TFAP2E/TMEM214 variants maternally inherited
quotes: In brief, the proband III-1 developed NB of the broad ligament at 17 months which was treated by surgery, radiation therapy and chemotherapy. At age 22 years, she developed a right PCC plus a ganglioneuroma at the site of the original NB and also an ileal schwannoma.

Six years later, the patient underwent adrenal surgery for a left PCC associated with a mature ganglioneuroma. At the same time, a well-differentiated leiomyosarcoma arising from the mesosigmoid was detected and surgically removed.
All also carried the MAX c.145T>C variant at the heterozygous level.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: I-1
quotes: Her paternal grandfather (I-1) had bilateral PCC at 70 years
Pre-operatively, patient I-1 had high urinary normetanephrines (5x the upper limit range) and chromogranin-A levels (x3 the upper limit range).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: II-3

phenotypes.text: adrenal nodule with high [18F]-DOPA uptake suggestive of pheochromocytoma

quotes: The MAX c.145T>C variant was also detected by Sanger sequencing at the heterozygous level in the germline DNA of the proband’s paternal uncle (II-3), who was KIF1B negative (Fig. 1).

Interestingly, II-3 recently developed, at age 56, a 11-mm hypervascular nodule in his right adrenal which remains clinically silent but strongly uptakes [18F]-DOPA during PET, suggestive of PCC or adrenomedullary nodule.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Family A

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 concentration

records.segregation: Identified in all individuals with PC and both children with neuroendocrine tumors; LOH in PC tissue
quotes: Family A has multiple individuals with PC (including bilateral and metastatic disease) and 2 children (to date, without PC) with neuroendocrine tumors (paravertebral ganglioneuroma and abdominal neuroblastoma, respectively). One individual has acromegaly; immunohistochemistry of PC tissue showed positive growth hormone-releasing hormone staining.

Another individual with previously resected PCs has pituitary enlargement and elevated insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1). A germline MAX variant (c.200C>A, p.Ala67Asp) was identified in all individuals with PC and both children, with loss of heterozygosity in PC tissue.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Family B proband
quotes: In Family B, the proband has bilateral and metastatic PC, prolactin-producing pituitary tumor, multigland parathyroid adenomas, chondrosarcoma, and multifocal pulmonary adenocarcinomas. A truncating germline MAX variant (c.22G>T, p.Glu8*) was identified.

records.label: FA-II-1

phenotypes.text: pituitary abnormalities or other neuroendocrine tumors

records.segregation: Parents (I-1, I-2) tested negative; carried by proband and his unaffected 13-year-old son
quotes: The proband ( Figures 1 -FA-II-1) was a 24-year-old man who had been diagnosed as having “right PCC” in December 2005 with more than a 2-year history of elevated blood pressure and a right adrenal mass detected 2 weeks previously.
Only the proband and his 13-year-old son ( Figures 1 -FA-III-1) carried a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 4 of MAX (p.R75*, c.223C>T; NM_002382.5; Figure 2A).
The final diagnosis was a metachronous bilateral PCC.

records.label: FB-II-1
quotes: The proband ( Figures 1 -FB-II-1), a 34-year-old male, was admitted to the hospital in December 2021 with bilateral adrenal lesions. He had no symptoms, such as headache, palpitations, or excessive sweating.
Plasma catecholamine, metanephrine, and normetanephrine levels were within normal limits.
the proband (FB-II-1) was found to carry a heterozygous frameshift mutation in exon 4 of MAX (p.Q82Tfs*89, c.242_243dupAC; NM_002382.5; Figure 2B).

records.label: FC-II-1
records.segregation: Variant also in one daughter and one sister, both without clinical or biochemical abnormalities
quotes: The proband ( Figures 1 -FC-II-1), a 64-year-old female, was admitted to our hospital in November 2022 with right adrenal lesions. She occasionally complained of paroxysmal headache.
In March 2024, genetic testing revealed a heterozygous missense mutation in exon 5 of MAX in the proband (p.E158A, c.473A>C; NM_002382.5; ( Figure 2C).

The mutation was detected in only one of her daughters and one of her sisters ( Figures 1 -FC-II-3, III-1), but their adrenal CT examination and blood biochemistry, such as plasma catecholamine, metanephrine, and normetanephrine, and so on, showed no abnormalities.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Propositus

phenotypes.text: mixed growth hormone-prolactin secreting pituitary macroadenoma

quotes: We identified a novel germline pathological variant in exon 4 of the MAX gene, c.228delG, which was predicted to lead to a truncated protein (p.Asn78Thrfs*92).
The propositus had developed pituitary gigantism due to a mixed growth hormone-prolactin secreting pituitary macroadenoma, which was controlled after two surgeries, medical therapy and radiotherapy.
He subsequently developed bilateral and recurrent pheochromocytomas and following his death, an extra-adrenal myelolipoma was identified that was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Affected relatives in the kindred
records.segregation: multiple affected and unaffected carriers of c.228delG identified in the kindred
quotes: An extensive history of pheochromocytomas or uncontrolled hypertension was present in the kindred and multiple affected and unaffected carriers of the c.228delG MAX pathogenic variant were characterized.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) reviewed MEN5 as a syndrome caused by inactivating variants in the MAX gene and characterized predominantly by high penetrance of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, with pituitary adenoma as a cardinal feature and parathyroid adenomas and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors as less common manifestations.
quotes: Inactivating variants of the MAX gene (chromosome 14q23.3; encoding MAX, a 160-amino acid transcription factor) produce MEN5 syndrome, designated by Seabrook et al. in 2021, following the association of MAX variants with PPGL since 2011.
Clinical data to date suggest that MEN5 syndrome is characterised predominantly by a high penetrance of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
MEN5 syndrome | MAX | PPGL, pituitary adenoma | Parathyroid adenomas, pancreatic NET | |

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that inactivating MAX variants prevent normal activation of the MYC-MAX heterodimer, leading to unregulated MYC function, and suggested that increased MYC activity may lead to a more aggressive subtype of neural crest chromaffin cells.
quotes: Inactivating MAX variants prevent normal activation of the MYC-MAX heterodimer, leading to unregulated MYC function and subsequent cell proliferation, differentiation and angiogenesis; it is thought that the increased MYC activity leads to the development of a more aggressive subtype of neural crest chromaffin cells.

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) summarized that pituitary adenomas associated with MAX variants tend to be functioning, typically of PIT1 lineage with GH and/or prolactin secretion, that pituitary gigantism has been reported, and that MAX-associated lactotroph adenomas respond well to dopamine agonists whereas somatotrophinomas often require multiple lines of therapy. The broader phenotype was hypothesized to include other neural crest-lineage tumors such as ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, chondrosarcoma, myelolipoma and lung adenocarcinoma.
quotes: Pituitary adenomas associated with MAX variants tend to be functioning, typically of PIT1 lineage with evidence of growth hormone and/or prolactin secretion.
MAX-associated lactotroph adenomas tend to respond well to dopamine agonist therapy, whereas MAX-associated somatotrophinoma tends to require multiple lines of therapy.

The broader phenotype of MAX variants has been hypothesised to additionally comprise other neural crest cell-lineage diseases, including ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, parathyroid adenomas, chondrosarcoma, myelolipoma and lung adenocarcinoma.

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) stated that the exact prevalence of MEN5 is unknown but that it is thought to account for 0.8 to 1.9% of pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas.
quotes: The exact prevalence of MEN5 syndrome is unknown, but it is thought to account for 0.8–1.9% of PPGL.

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that loss of MAX immunohistochemical staining and loss of heterozygosity have been identified in MAX-related pheochromocytoma and suggested these tests may help when a germline MAX variant of uncertain significance is found; the catecholamine phenotype is generally mixed noradrenaline and adrenaline secretion.
quotes: Both loss of immunohistochemical staining for MAX and loss of heterozygosity have been identified in MAX-related phaeochromocytoma; thus, such tests may be pursued in clinical settings suspicious for a causative MAX variant, e.g. in the case of a germline MAX variant of uncertain significance.
Screening with supine plasma metanephrines is essential, with the catecholamine phenotype generally being mixed noradrenaline and adrenaline secretion.

notes.statement: Maggacis et al. (2026) noted that there are no formal consensus surveillance guidelines for MEN5, but that a pediatric PPGL consensus recommended annual clinical assessment from age 10 years and annual plasma metanephrines with MRI of neck to pelvis every 2 to 3 years from presentation or age 15 years for carriers of pathogenic germline MAX variants.
quotes: Critically, there are no formal guidelines regarding comprehensive MEN5 surveillance; however, an international consensus statement regarding childhood PPGL management recommended that surveillance for those with a known pathogenic germline MAX variant should include annual clinical assessment from the age of 10 years, and annual plasma metanephrines and 2–3 yearly MRI neck to pelvis from presentation or from the age of 15 years.

notes.statement: In a systematic review of 45 studies covering 127 patients with germline MAX mutations, Charoenngam et al. (2026) found a median age at first tumor diagnosis of 29 years; 37.0% of patients were women. The most frequent tumors were pheochromocytoma (112 patients), pituitary adenoma (11), and paraganglioma (10), with median ages at diagnosis of 31.0, 33.0, and 43.0 years, respectively.
quotes: Of 621 records screened, 45 studies comprising 127 patients with germline MAX mutations met the eligibility criteria. The median age at first tumor diagnosis was 29 years (23.0 - 39.0) and 37.0% were women.
The most frequent tumors were pheochromocytoma (PCC, N = 112), pituitary adenoma (N = 11), and paraganglioma (N = 10), with median ages at diagnosis of 31.0, 33.0, and 43.0 years, respectively.

notes.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) found that 38.3% of pheochromocytomas in MEN5 were unilateral and 27.6% were metastatic. Most of the tumors secreted norepinephrine.
quotes: Among PCCs, 38.3% were unilateral, 27.6% were metastatic, and most were norepinephrine-secreting.

notes.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) found evidence that loss of MAX contributes to the development of paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, renal oncocytoma, myelolipoma, and liver sarcoma. Whether MAX loss causes primary hyperparathyroidism remained uncertain.
quotes: Evidence implicating MAX loss in tumorigenesis included paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, renal oncocytoma, myelolipoma, and liver sarcoma.
The causal association between primary hyperparathyroidism and MAX loss remains uncertain.

notes.statement: Charoenngam et al. (2026) described MEN5 as a newly recognized entity caused by heterozygous inactivating germline mutations in MAX. They noted that its epidemiology, penetrance, and genotype-phenotype associations had not yet been defined.
quotes: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 5 (MEN5) caused by heterozygous inactivating germline MYC-associated factor X (MAX) mutations
further studies are needed to define the epidemiology, penetrance and genotype-phenotype associations of this newly recognized entity

notes.statement: In the propositus of a MEN5 kindred with a germline MAX c.228delG variant, Haider et al. (2025) found that an extra-adrenal myelolipoma identified after his death was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry, and they characterized myelolipoma as a new disease association in MEN5.
quotes: following his death, an extra-adrenal myelolipoma was identified that was negative on MAX immunohistochemistry
characterize myeloplipoma as a new disease-association in MEN5

notes.statement: Haider et al. (2025) reported the first case of pituitary gigantism associated with a pathogenic MAX variant. They suggested that comprehensive screening of MAX pathogenic variant carriers could help identify rare disease associations beyond pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma.
quotes: We report the first case of pituitary gigantism in association with a pathogenic variant in the MAX gene
comprehensive screening of MAX pathogenic variant carriers can help to identify rare disease associations beyond PPGL.

notes.statement: In a review of 109 carriers of germline MAX mutations from 87 families (6 new and 103 previously reported), Lian et al. (2024) found that 101 (92.7%) developed pheochromocytoma at a mean age of 32.8 years (range, 13-80), 59 of which were bilateral; 19 (18.8%) had metastatic disease and 11 (10.9%) had concomitant thoracic or abdominal paraganglioma.
quotes: Overall, 101 (92.7%) of the 109 patients developed PCC, with a mean age at diagnosis of 32.8 ± 12.6 years (range, 13–80), and the male-to-female ratio was 1.3:1. Of these, 59 (58.4%) developed bilateral PCC
Nineteen (18.8%) of the patients were diagnosed with metastatic PCC. Eleven (10.9%) had concomitant chest or abdominal PGL, and one presented with head and neck PGL without PCC.

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) found that 9 (8.3%) of 109 MAX mutation carriers had functional pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (growth hormone- and/or prolactin-secreting), and 11 (10.1%) had other neuroendocrine tumors including primary hyperparathyroidism, neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglioneuroma, C-cell hyperplasia, and pancreatic NET; 7 had non-neuroendocrine tumors of uncertain relation.
quotes: Overall, nine (8.3%) patients were complicated with pituitary NET (PitNET). Among them, three, four, and one patient had a single increase in growth hormone, prolactin, and both hormone and prolactin concentrations, respectively

Eleven (10.1%) developed other NETs, with an age at diagnosis ranging from 0.7 to 60 years, including seven combined with PCC: four primary hyperparathyroidism(PHPT) cases and each of one case in neuroblastoma, pelvic ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglionoma, and C-cell hyperplasia.

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) noted that among 63 MAX-associated pheochromocytoma patients with catecholamine data, 61 (96.8%) were positive, 70.5% of them showing a mixed noradrenergic/adrenergic secretion pattern rather than isolated norepinephrine elevation.
quotes: The results showed that 61 (96.8%) were positive, of which 18 (29.5%) were positive for an increase in a single normetanephrine/norepinephrine and 43 (70.5%) were positive for a mixed increase in metanephrine/adrenaline, normetanephrine/norepinephrine, and/or dopamine.

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) tabulated 53 distinct germline MAX alterations involving all 5 exons; the most frequent were p.R33* (21.1%), p.R75* (13.8%), and p.A67D (7.3%), and nonsense mutations predominated (47.7%).
quotes: The three most common mutations were p.R33* (c.97C>T; 21.1%), p.R75* (c.223C>T; 13.8%), and p.A67D (c.200C>A; 7.3%).
Of the 53 MAX germline alterations identified, the most common mutations were nonsense mutations (47.7%), followed by missense mutations (23.8%)

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) found no significant differences in age at diagnosis or occurrence of pheochromocytoma, metastasis, paraganglioma, pituitary adenoma, or other tumors between carriers of missense and nonmissense MAX mutations, suggesting a weak genotype-phenotype correlation.
quotes: The results indicated that the high penetrance of MAX mutation-related PCC and relatively high metastatic risk may not be related to MAX mutation types, or that the genotype-phenotype correlation is not strong.

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) noted that only 22 (25.3%) of 87 MAX mutation pedigrees had a family history of PPGL and suggested that de novo MAX mutations may be common; 3 of 109 carriers had no clinical phenotype.
quotes: Among the 87 families, 22 (25.3%) had a family history of PPGL and eight (9.2%) had a clear paternal family genetic background.
MAX mutations may also have a very high de novo mutation rate (65.8%), and de novo MAX mutations may be a common pathogenic form.

notes.statement: Lian et al. (2024) proposed that MAX germline mutations cause a new type of multiple endocrine neoplasia originating from the neural crest, which may be called MEN5, and recommended comprehensive baseline assessment of carriers for PPGL, pituitary adenoma, hyperparathyroidism, and ganglioneuroma/neuroblastoma.
quotes: In conclusion, MAX germline mutations may cause a new type of MEN originating from the neural crest, which may be called MEN 5.

This suggests that all MAX germline mutation carriers should receive a comprehensive baseline assessment of the diversity of neurocrest-derived diseases, such as PPGL, PA, hyperparathyroidism, and ganglioneuroma/neuroblastoma.

notes.statement: In a review, Sahakian et al. (2024) noted that recently described families carrying a MAX mutation, which predisposes to pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, showed a phenotypic spectrum evoking multiple endocrine neoplasia. They said this suggested the existence of another syndrome, MEN5.
quotes: the recent description of families carrying a mutation in MAX, which is known to predispose to the development of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, and presents a phenotypic spectrum that evokes MEN, suggests the existence of another syndrome, MEN5.

notes.statement: Sahakian et al. (2024) stated that the multiple endocrine neoplasia syndromes are a group with a genetic predisposition to endocrine tumors and show autosomal dominant transmission.
quotes: Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) is a group of syndromes with a genetic predisposition to the appearance of endocrine tumors, and shows autosomal dominant transmission.

notes.statement: Nosé et al. (2022) reviewed the fifth edition of the WHO Classification of Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Tumors and described MEN5, together with MAFA-related syndrome and MEN4, as a newly defined familial cancer syndrome.
quotes: We describe the newly defined Familial Cancer Syndromes as MAFA-related, MEN4, and MEN5 as well as the newly reported pathological findings in DICER1 syndrome.

notes.statement: Seabrook et al. (2021) found loss of MAX immunohistochemical staining in pheochromocytomas and other neural crest tumors from Family A, and in vitro studies confirmed the p.Ala67Asp MAX variant as loss of function.
quotes: Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MAX staining in PCs and other neural crest tumors. In vitro studies confirmed the variant as loss of function.

notes.statement: Seabrook et al. (2021) concluded that germline MAX mutations are associated with pheochromocytomas, ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, and possibly parathyroid adenomas, as well as chondrosarcoma and lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting that MAX is a novel multiple endocrine neoplasia gene.
quotes: Germline MAX mutations are associated with PCs, ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, and, possibly, parathyroid adenomas, as well as nonendocrine tumors of chondrosarcoma and lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting MAX is a novel multiple endocrine neoplasia gene.

notes.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) concluded that heritability of pheochromocytoma in a family previously attributed to a KIF1B variant was linked to a germline MAX p.Ser49Pro variant, supported by a normetanephrine-predominant secretory pattern, loss of the wildtype MAX allele in both pheochromocytomas of one carrier, and structural modeling predicting the proline substitution to be incompatible with native conformation.
quotes: In this family, the heritability of PCC is linked to the MAX germline variant and not to the KIF1B germline variant
The p.Ser49Pro MAX variant is predicted to show the Proline 49 with an opened cycle which is impossible, leading probably to the precipitation of the protein (Fig. 2).

notes.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) noted incomplete penetrance of the MAX variant, as the father of the proband carried it without developing any adrenal lesion on repeated imaging and biochemical follow-up.
quotes: We propose that in this family the genetic susceptibility to PCC/PGL is linked to the MAX nucleotide variant which is however associated with an incomplete penetrance since patient II-2 did not develop any symptomatic adrenal lesion.

notes.statement: Cardot Bauters et al. (2020) observed increased urinary normetanephrines with normal total metanephrines in a MAX variant carrier with bilateral pheochromocytoma, a pattern reminiscent of MAX-related tumors.
quotes: The secretory profile of his tumors consisted of increased urinary normetanephrines at 1979 nmol/mmol of creatinine (8x the upper limit range) with normal total metanephrines at 182 nmol/mmol of creatinine (<190), reminiscent of the pattern observed in patients with a MAX pathogenic variant.

notes.statement: Taïeb et al. (2018) found that 18F-FDOPA PET/CT accurately visualized MAX-related pheochromocytomas, which were often multiple or bilateral, with a per-lesion sensitivity of 90.9% versus 52.4% for CT/MRI. 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT detected fewer lesions in 1 of 3 patients, and 18F-FDG PET/CT was only faintly positive in 2 of 4 patients. The authors recommended 18F-FDOPA PET/CT as the first-line functional imaging modality for these patients.
quotes: In all cases, 18F-FDOPA PET/CT accurately visualized PHEOs that were often multiple within the same gland or bilaterally and detected more adrenal and extra-adrenal lesions than did CT (per-lesion sensitivity, 90.9% vs 52.4% for CT/magnetic resonance imaging).
68Ga-DOTA,Tyr3-octreotate PET/CT detected fewer lesions than did 18F-FDOPA PET/CT in one of three patients, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT was only faintly positive in two of four patients
18F-FDOPA PET/CT should be considered as the first-line functional imaging modality for diagnostic or follow-up evaluations for these patients.

notes.statement: In silico analyses by Taïeb et al. (2018) predicted that the 5 different MAX mutations in their patients disrupted the Max/Myc interaction and/or abolished interaction with DNA.
quotes: The patients had five different mutations in the MAX gene that caused disruption of Max/Myc interaction and/or abolished interaction with DNA based on in silico analyses.

notes.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) sequenced the exomes of 3 unrelated individuals with hereditary pheochromocytoma and identified mutations in the MAX gene. Absence of MAX protein in the tumors and loss of heterozygosity caused by uniparental disomy supported the involvement of MAX in the disease; a follow-up study of 59 selected cases identified 5 additional MAX mutations.
quotes: We sequenced the exomes of three unrelated individuals with hereditary PCC (cases) and identified mutations in MAX, the MYC associated factor X gene.
Absence of MAX protein in the tumors and loss of heterozygosity caused by uniparental disomy supported the involvement of MAX alterations in the disease.

notes.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) suggested preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations in hereditary pheochromocytoma.
quotes: suggested an association with malignant outcome and preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations

notes.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) suggested that MAX mutations were associated with malignant outcome of pheochromocytoma and that loss of MAX function is correlated with metastatic potential.
quotes: suggested an association with malignant outcome and preferential paternal transmission of MAX mutations
suggests that loss of MAX function is correlated with metastatic potential

notes.statement: Comino-Méndez et al. (2011) noted that involvement of the MYC-MAX-MXD1 network in neural crest cell tumors was supported by the lack of functional MAX in rat PCC (PC12) cells and by MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma.
quotes: The involvement of the MYC-MAX-MXD1 network in the development and progression of neural crest cell tumors is further supported by the lack of functional MAX in rat PCC (PC12) cells and by the amplification of MYCN in neuroblastoma

notes.statement: Using an unbiased shRNA screen, Schlisio et al. (2008) found that the kinesin KIF1B-beta acts downstream of the EglN3 prolyl hydroxylase. They found it was both necessary and sufficient for neuronal apoptosis when nerve growth factor (NGF) becomes limiting. This places it in the developmental apoptotic pathway on which VHL, NF1, RET, SDHB, and SDHD act.
quotes: Using an unbiased shRNA screen we found that the kinesin KIF1Bbeta acts downstream from EglN3 and is both necessary and sufficient for neuronal apoptosis when NGF becomes limiting.

VHL, NF-1, c-Ret, and Succinate Dehydrogenase Subunits B and D act on a developmental apoptotic pathway that is activated when nerve growth factor (NGF) becomes limiting for neuronal progenitor cells and requires the EglN3 prolyl hydroxylase as a downstream effector.

notes.statement: Schlisio et al. (2008) noted that KIF1B-beta maps to chromosome 1p36.2, a region frequently deleted in neural crest-derived tumors. They identified inherited loss-of-function KIF1B-beta missense mutations in neuroblastomas and pheochromocytomas, and an acquired loss-of-function mutation in a medulloblastoma. They argued that KIF1B-beta is a pathogenic target of 1p36 deletions.
quotes: KIF1Bbeta maps to chromosome 1p36.2, which is frequently deleted in neural crest-derived tumors including neuroblastomas.

We identified inherited loss-of-function KIF1Bbeta missense mutations in neuroblastomas and pheochromocytomas and an acquired loss-of-function mutation in a medulloblastoma, arguing that KIF1Bbeta is a pathogenic target of these deletions.
